title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page sketches the Steenrod–Dold construction of the reduced power operations. It sits in an 'EZ' (Eilenberg–Zilber) sequence of notes. The previous page covered shuffle and Alexander–Whitney maps, their associativity and (homotopy) commutativity, and Dold's theorem that Hom^•(Z(X^n), Z(X)^{⊗n}) is a free Σ_n-resolution of Z.

The steps, in modern language:
1. Take a class f ∈ H^n(X, A), with A essentially F_p.
2. Form the external p-th power f^{×p} on X^p. Using the Σ_p-equivariance supplied by the acyclic-models / Dold resolution, it extends to an equivariant class Pf ∈ H^{pn}_{Σ_p}(EΣ_p × X^p, A). This is the cohomology of the extended power EΣ_p ×_{Σ_p} X^p.
3. Pull back along the diagonal X → X^p, which is Σ_p-invariant. This gives ΔPf ∈ H^{pn}(BΣ_p × X, A).
4. Over F_p, the Künneth formula gives H^*(K(Σ_p,1) × X) = H^*(K(Σ_p,1)) ⊗_{F_p} H^*(X, A).
5. Pair with homology classes e_α ∈ H_α(K(Σ_p,1)). This yields the components D_i x ∈ H^{pn−i}(X, A), so that ΔPf = Σ_i w_i ⊗ D_i f.
6. The Steenrod powers are then P^i x = (±) D_{f(i)} (times a unit), for a suitable reindexing f(i) = (n−2i)(p−1) or similar. The note records that this reindexing (with signs) is what makes the Cartan formula take its clean form.
7. In practice one restricts to the cyclic subgroup Z/p ⊂ Σ_p and uses cyclic group cohomology. That subgroup is a p-Sylow subgroup, and the restriction is injective on mod-p cohomology.

This is exactly the textbook treatment of Steenrod–Epstein, 'Cohomology Operations', Ch. VII. It reads as lecture or reading notes recalling background on Steenrod operations. They likely serve the divided-power / décalage discussion on the next page (Quillen–Illusie décalage for derived functors of Sym, Λ, Γ).
errors: Pf is written in H_{Σ_n}^{pn}(EΣ_n × X^p, A). The group should be Σ_p, not Σ_n; n is the cohomological degree. This is a slip.
The Künneth identification ⊗_{F_p} requires A = F_p (or a field of characteristic p). The page writes general A.
The sign exponent (−1)^{( )} and the reindexing function f(i) are left unspecified. The standard normalization also includes a unit factor (e.g. (m!)^ε with m = (p−1)/2) beyond a sign.
Strictly, the Cartan formula comes from multiplicativity of the external power construction. The reindexing only makes it take the standard form P^k(xy) = Σ P^i x P^{k−i} y.

A struck-out symbol (looks like e_α or 'Σ_p H' scribble) appears under the Künneth line near the ⊗_{F_p}. It is crossed out and is not a separate formula.
